name: alarm
description: The alarm tool's whole lifecycle in one pass: set must persist a reminder and return its id, list must show it as pending with due:false, done on a recurring alarm must advance it instead of deleting it, cancel must remove outright, and the final list must come back empty. Exercises the tool's CAS read-modify-write path against state/alarms.json end to end — application logic no build gate touches. It goes red when set stops persisting, ids stop round-tripping, recurrence stops advancing, or the stale-hash retry loop breaks. The eval's staging state dir starts empty, so the final empty list is deterministic.
prompt: Use the alarm tool six times, in order: (1) {"action":"set","message":"eval reminder","in_minutes":60}; note the id. (2) {"action":"list"} — the alarm is present with due false. (3) {"action":"set","message":"eval recurring","in_minutes":0,"every_minutes":30}; note its id. (4) {"action":"done","id":"<id from step 3>"} — expect ok true and a next_in_seconds near 1800, meaning it advanced rather than vanished. (5) {"action":"cancel","id":"<id from step 1>"} and {"action":"cancel","id":"<id from step 3>"}. (6) {"action":"list"} — the alarms array is now empty. If every step behaved as described, reply with exactly CLEAN. Otherwise reply with exactly BROKEN and one sentence naming the failing step.
